title: sse-partial-json-delimiter-token-ordering-fix
author: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Fixes multiple edge cases in the SSE streaming path where partial JSON payloads and delimiter tokens could be emitted in an order that made downstream OpenAI-compatible clients (and our function/tool-calling handlers) parse invalid or truncated JSON objects. This PR addresses token/event ordering invariants, stabilizes chunk framing for partial JSON, and hardens the OpenAI compatibility adapter to accept both legacy and corrected delimiter placements. Motivation: We have observed production incidents and flaky e2e test failures when long streaming responses are chunked such that the partial-JSON delimiter (e.g. '\n\n' or explicit 'DELIM_JSON') lands between token events. That caused the consumer to see delimiter + fragment in the wrong order (token event after a delimiter) which broke our structured output / function-calling parsing pipeline (SUP-4821, ENG-1124). Changes: 1) Enforce a strict emission invariant in the streaming runtime: delimiter markers are emitted immediately before the first token of a partial JSON fragment; token events for that fragment cannot interleave with delimiter events. 2) Update chunking algorithm to produce deterministic framing headers for partial JSON (framing metadata embedded in SSE comment lines, not as tokens). 3) Add an explicit flush/commit semantics when switching from natural token streaming to structured partial-JSON modes to avoid cross-chunk buffering. 4) OpenAI compatibility layer: accept both delimiter-before-token and delimiter-as-comment placements for backward compatibility, log a one-time warning if legacy ordering is detected. 5) Add targeted unit and integration tests that simulate race conditions (high token throughput + deliberate small chunk sizes) and a new e2e test validating function/tool-calling when partial JSON payloads are split across multiple SSE events. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce failing scenario in test harness - [x] Implement runtime invariant enforcement - [x] Update OpenAI compat adapter with compatibility handling and warning - [x] Add unit/integration/e2e tests - [x] Run CI and fix lint/test failures Notes on implementation: The core change is in the framer (runtime/streaming/sse_framer.py) and the Rust parser (runtime/streaming/sse_parser.rs) which now coordinate via a small stable header (comment) preceding partial JSON fragments. The header uses a compact encoding (type=partial_json;id=...) to avoid relying on token boundary semantics. The Node/TS and Go OpenAI-compat adapters were updated to treat this header as authoritative for when to start aggregating JSON fragments. Observability: added two new metrics (streaming.partial_json.reorders and streaming.partial_json.flushes) and an alert rule to detect regression in reorders. Backwards compatibility: unchanged for most clients; compatibility adapter handles legacy cases. Risk: low-medium - touches hot path but guarded by unit tests and staged rollout. Related: ENG-1189 (streaming perf), SUP-4821.

review_comments: Diego: Can we make the delimiter invariant explicit in code (assertion) and add a debug-only check so we can detect regressions?
Asha: Added a runtime-only invariant check behind a feature flag and a test that simulates cross-chunk buffering. Leaving disabled by default in prod; can be enabled for canary telemetry.
Emily: Nice catch on the parser state machine; please add a test exercising function/tool-calling payloads split across more than 3 events.
Asha: Added e2e test that splits a function-arguments JSON object across 5 small SSE events and validated the compat adapter, included in this PR.
Nikhil: Approving with one small nit: prefer constants for the header keys (applied inline).
release_notes: Fixed SSE streaming chunking/framing bug that caused partial-JSON delimiter/token ordering issues; improves stability for structured output and function/tool-calling over streaming. Backwards-compatible adapter included.
